_about: Look profiles (Technical Artist, 2026-10-08, the grim look test). Switch with F11 in the PSX options overlay (auto, classic, grim). A scene picks its own profile from scene_defaults unless the overlay forced one. 'classic' is the toy-box look Ross approved first and is never changed; it stays one F11 press away. GRIM IS THE DEFAULT EVERYWHERE since Ross approved the look test (2026-10-08). 'grim' is the greasy, desaturated, oppressive look from Ross's 2026-10-08 tone decision ('desaturate, darken, grime things up a bit'). Read by scripts/core/look_profiles.gd; every key has a test. grade.* feed the PSX post shader (shaders/psx_post.gdshader); post.* are its color levels and dither size; lighting.* are multipliers on a room's own ambient and lights (PsxRoomLook); fog.* tint and shorten the fog; materials.* drain and darken room material tints (GrimDressing); grime.* are the code-painted grime colors and amounts (GrimePaint); characters.* is the dull, matte, scuffed pass on character textures; models maps a classic model path to this profile's variant; backdrop.* replaces keys of the battle set (BattleBackdrop). 'grim_ps2' (added 2026-10-08, Technical Artist) is the early-PS2 look for the combat sandbox: see its own _about; it is never anyone's default.

scene_defaults._note: Which profile a scene gets on its own, if it should differ from 'default'. Keys are room ids (data/world/rooms.json) or 'battle'. Empty: grim everywhere since Ross approved it (2026-10-08). F11 in the overlay forces any profile on every scene.

grade._note: amount 1 = fully on. desat drains colour (accent_keep spares bright saturated pixels: lamps, warning stripes, the call's teal). crush/gamma/gain darken. The split tone pushes shadows teal and highlights sodium orange.

characters._note: Characters and enemies: dulled (unless prepainted), then lifted so they read against the dark set, plus an edge light (rim_*, psx_lit.gdshader). roles.<party|enemy|npc> lay over the base block. Ross, 2026-10-08: brighter to stand out, 'not too bright though - edgelight'.

player_lamp._note: Red carries her lamp: a small warm light that rides with her in the grim look.

grim_ps2.name: Grim PS2 (combat sandbox)

grade._note: Ross's 'B filter' (2026-10-08): a lighter grade than grim (desat 0.35 not 0.75, tint 0.3 not 0.6, gamma 1.0 not 1.1); grain, vignette, crush and accent_keep as in grim.

fog._note: A gentle haze at long range, for mood only: it never hides distance (Ross, 2026-10-08: long draw distances are a modern convenience we keep). PsxRoomLook (the sandbox's room look) scales its 12 m / 24 m by near_mul and far_mul, giving 30 m to 150 m; near_m and far_m are the same numbers for scenes without one (Ps2Look). Nothing in the arena (44 m across) is more than a few percent fogged.

characters._note: Ross's own art is NEVER repainted (dull false, no prepainted list): only the edge light and a small lift for readability. Edge light stays 'not too bright' (F56); the glow threshold sits above it so it never blooms. by_model keys match the model path.

player_lamp._note: Red carries her lamp: a small warm light that rides with her in the grim look.

grim_ps2._about: The early-PS2 look for the combat sandbox (Ross, 2026-10-08: 'the psx look needs a upgrade to ps2'; docs/pivot/combat_api.md section 6). Grim's grade, fog and edge light kept; 640x360 smooth picture, retro wobble (vertex jitter, affine warp), dither and 15-bit colour off, a real-time key-light shadow, glow, gentle smooth fog. Applied by scripts/core/ps2_look.gd (a look-aware node the sandbox adds); a scene without that node only gets the grade and fog. texture_filter is per texture group: smooth (linear + mipmaps) or nearest (crisp pixels); Ross has not chosen for the city tiles yet, so they stay nearest.

screen._note: The internal picture size is a data setting (psx_look.json lists the sizes); Ross may revisit it.

shadows._note: One key light; modern quality where it is cheap: four stable cascades out to 60 m (the whole arena), blended seams, a medium soft filter, a 4096 atlas. No shimmer from a short distance.

texture_filter._note: smooth = linear with mipmaps; nearest = crisp pixels. Groups: characters (Red, NPCs), enemies, weapons, placeholders (the old blockouts), city_tiles (Ross's pixel-art floor and wall tiles: nearest 'for now', Ross 2026-10-08; he may change it, so it stays a data setting), default.

camera._note: No draw-distance limit for authenticity: the far plane is long and nothing pops in.
